title: Fabrication of Monocrystalline Thin Semiconductor via Crack-Assisted Layer Exfoliation
author: Lee, Gupta, et al.
materials: Platinum counter electrode for Ni electrodeposition

A number of approaches can be used to form the stressor layer on the Si donor substrate. For instance, sputter and electroplating processes are generally used in the crack-assisted layer exfoliation method (Lee et al., 2020). In this protocol, we used the electroplating process due to the highly controllability of the stress level and high deposition rates in a simple solution-based processing, whereas the sputter process demands complex vacuum processing technology. In the electroplating process, the residual stress of the deposited Ni stressor layer is strongly affected by the composition of electroplating solution. Especially, NiCl2 solution is known to form Ni thin films with high residual stress. In the following steps, we describe the preparation of NiCl2 based electroplating solutions.1.Dissolve 22 g of H3BO3 powder into 600 mL of deionized (DI) water (obtained using Millipore DI water purification system) in a glass beaker under magnetic stirring. Stirring should be continued until the solution turns transparent without any precipitates.2.Add 86 g of nickel chloride hexahydrate (NiCl2·6H2O) into the mixed solution under constant magnetic stirring for more than 12 h until the solution turns green without any undissolved precipitates. Use parafilm to cover the glass beaker containing the mixed solution to avoid water evaporation.

steps.title: Prepare NiCl₂ electroplating bath
steps.instruction: Prepare the nickel electroplating solution (timing ≈ 1 day) as follows:

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 22 g of H₃BO₃ powder in 600 mL of deionized water in a glass beaker while stirring magnetically; continue stirring until the solution becomes transparent and free of precipitates.
Add 86 g of nickel chloride hexahydrate (NiCl₂·6H₂O) to the mixture, keep magnetic stirring for more than 12 h until the solution turns green and no undissolved particles remain.
Cover the beaker with parafilm to prevent water evaporation.

steps.title: Secure Si donor substrate
steps.instruction: Fix the Ni‑stressor‑layer‑deposited Si donor wafer onto a flat surface (e.g., lab bench) by attaching scotch tape to its edges (timing ≈ 10 min).

steps.title: Initiate crack propagation
steps.instruction: Using a curved‑sharp‑tip tweezer, grasp the locally exfoliated thin Si attached to the Ni stressor layer and pull vertically to start crack propagation.

steps.title: Complete exfoliation of thin Si
steps.instruction: Continue applying a steady, non‑abrupt pulling force until the crack reaches the opposite edge of the initial crack, resulting in full separation of the Si thin film (with Ni stressor layer) from the donor substrate.

substeps.instruction: Maintain a constant pulling speed; avoid sudden high forces that increase fracture‑surface roughness.
Ensure the Ni stressor layer thickness exceeds the critical thickness required for crack initiation (thickness can be increased by longer electroplating time or higher current density).
